identity.name: Riograndense Republic
alt_names: Republic of Rio Grande do Sul

land.text: the Province of São Pedro do Rio Grande do Sul, partly split off

predecessors.note: The Empire of Brazil dossier records the matching loss on 11 September 1836.

land.text: the republic 'reincorporated into the Brazilian Empire' as the province of Rio Grande do Sul

successors.note: Cliopatria returns the land to the Empire's shape in 1846.

capitals.name: Piratini
capitals.note: The page names five capitals (Piratini, Alegrete, Caçapava do Sul, with Bagé briefly and São Borja) without dating them; 'The capital was also established in the small city of Piratini', and the constitution's signing line reads Piratini, 29 August 1838. Piratini is held to 1842 only because no other seat is dated before 1843.

capitals.name: Alegrete
capitals.note: The constitution was signed at Alegrete on 8 February 1843; the end year is the treaty's.

rulers.name: Bento Gonçalves da Silva
rulers.title: president
rulers.note: First president; 'took office on 6 November 1836' (infobox 1836-1841); imprisoned in Bahia in 1841.

rulers.name: José Gomes de Vasconcelos Jardim
rulers.title: president
rulers.note: The page says he succeeded Gonçalves in 1841 and gives no term end; the strip runs to the treaty of 1845 by default.

correction.text: the Province of São Pedro do Rio Grande do Sul without Porto Alegre: the republic's 'territory derived from the partial split' of the province, and the empire 'kept' Porto Alegre 'for the rest of the war'

keyframe_review.note: 287,825 km2 for 1836-1841: the modern state of Rio Grande do Sul (98% of its cells; about 281,700 km2, ratio 1.02) with border slivers of Uruguay (Artigas, Cerro Largo, Rivera, Rocha) and Argentina that no page gives the republic. The Ragamuffin War page: rebels seized Porto Alegre on 20 September 1835 but 'Porto Alegre had been recaptured by the empire in June 1836' and the empire kept it to the end, so the corrected shape drops the capital's cell(s) and the foreign slivers. The Riograndense page adds that the territory 'derived from the partial split of the Province' and that the Imperial Navy held the Patos Lagoon; neither page says which side held Rio Grande, Pelotas or the interior towns, so the rest of the province stays the republic's claim, drawn as contested in the ledger. No page gives an area.

correction.text: the Province of São Pedro do Rio Grande do Sul without Porto Alegre: the republic's 'territory derived from the partial split' of the province, and the empire 'kept' Porto Alegre 'for the rest of the war'

keyframe_review.note: The same outline for 1842-1845 (287,825 km2) with the same correction. The Ragamuffin War page records no territorial change after 1839: the rebels 'issued a republican constitution' in 1842 (the Riograndense page dates the signing at Alegrete to 8 February 1843) and Lima e Silva took imperial command that year.

region.text: the Province of São Pedro do Rio Grande do Sul without Porto Alegre: the republic's 'territory derived from the partial split' of the province, and the empire 'kept' Porto Alegre 'for the rest of the war'

ledger.note: 1836: the Riograndense Republic is proclaimed. 'It was proclaimed on 11 September 1836 by general Antônio de Sousa Neto' after the victory at Seival; Bento Gonçalves 'took office on 6 November 1836' as first president.

region.text: the Province of São Pedro do Rio Grande do Sul without Porto Alegre: the republic's 'territory derived from the partial split' of the province, and the empire 'kept' Porto Alegre 'for the rest of the war'

ledger.note: 1836: the republic and the empire dispute the province. The Ragamuffin War is dated 1835-1845 (infobox); the empire's navy held the Patos Lagoon, and the page does not say which side held Porto Alegre, Rio Grande or Pelotas, so the whole province is drawn as contested. The empire-of-brazil dossier dates the rising to 20 September 1835.

region.text: Laguna in Santa Catarina, taken by the Riograndense navy and land force on 22 July 1839, and the Juliana Republic proclaimed around it

ledger.note: 1839: the Riograndense navy takes Laguna in Santa Catarina. 'Laguna was taken' on 22 July 1839 (Garibaldi and Canabarro); the infobox gives 24 July 1839 for the confederation with the Juliana Republic, which 'was proclaimed an independent country' on 29 July.

region.text: Laguna in Santa Catarina, taken by the Riograndense navy and land force on 22 July 1839, and the Juliana Republic proclaimed around it

ledger.note: 1839: the empire retakes Laguna. 'The retaking of Laguna on 1 November 1839 put an end to the Juliana Republic'; the Riograndense navy had been 'completely destroyed in 1839'.

region.text: the Province of São Pedro do Rio Grande do Sul without Porto Alegre: the republic's 'territory derived from the partial split' of the province, and the empire 'kept' Porto Alegre 'for the rest of the war'

ledger.note: 1845: peace. 'Finally, on 1 March 1845, peace was signed: the Ponche Verde Treaty, after almost ten years of war'; complete amnesty for the rebels, freedom for the slaves who fought in the Republican Army. The Ragamuffin War page has it signed at Dom Pedrito, with the rebels choosing the next provincial president and the empire paying the republic's debts.

region.text: the Province of São Pedro do Rio Grande do Sul without Porto Alegre: the republic's 'territory derived from the partial split' of the province, and the empire 'kept' Porto Alegre 'for the rest of the war'

ledger.note: 1845: the republic ends. Under the Ponche Verde Treaty it 'was reincorporated into the Brazilian Empire', and the rebels could elect a new provincial president.

Laguna in Santa Catarina, taken by the Riograndense navy and land force on 22 July 1839, and the Juliana Republic proclaimed around it

wars.outcome: Negotiated end: the Ponche Verde Treaty of 1 March 1845 gave the rebels complete amnesty and reincorporated the republic into the Empire of Brazil; the Juliana Republic had been crushed when Laguna was retaken on 1 November 1839.
wars.note: Infobox 1835-1845; result 'Imperial victory'; territorial changes 'The Juliana and Riograndense Republics were dissolved and reintegrated into the Empire'; peace signed at Dom Pedrito. The republic's navy under Garibaldi (captain-lieutenant from 1 September 1838) was destroyed in 1839; Uruguay 'started to recognize' the republic but the process was not completed; the page also says the United Kingdom and France recognised it with a condition on port access, against the infobox 'Unrecognized state'.

certainty.note: The republic's territory was a 'partial split' of the province whose limits with Uruguay were 'fully defined only after the war'; which towns each side held is not on the page.

sources.title: Riograndense Republic
sources.note: Identity, proclamation (11 September 1836), capitals, presidents, the Laguna expedition and Juliana Republic (22 July - 1 November 1839), Ponche Verde (1 March 1845); read twice for the territory question.

sources.title: Ragamuffin War
sources.note: Porto Alegre seized 20 September 1835 and recaptured June 1836 and kept by the empire; the 1839 Juliana Republic; the 1842 constitution; the peace of 1 March 1845 at Dom Pedrito; Uruguay's support.

notes: Two pages (the Riograndense Republic page read twice, then the Ragamuffin War page). Not settled: (1) What land the rebels held: the Riograndense page says the territory was a 'partial split' of the province and that the Imperial Navy held the Patos Lagoon, the Ragamuffin War page that the empire kept Porto Alegre (recaptured June 1836); the pages are silent on Rio Grande, Pelotas and the interior towns, so the shape is the province minus Porto Alegre, kept as the claim and drawn as contested with the empire (the empire-of-brazil dossier has the matching contest from 1835). (2) Capitals: five, undated except Piratini (29 August 1838 signing) and Alegrete (constitution, 8 February 1843); the dossier's two spans are bridges, not facts. (3) The Juliana Republic (July-November 1839, Laguna and the Santa Catarina coast, four months) held land for less than a year and has no Cliopatria row: it needs a short dossier (am-08-x) or stays a footnote. (4) Type is 'rebel' (an unrecognised breakaway republic, like the Confederacy); the infobox says 'Unrecognized state'. (5) Cliopatria returns the land to the Empire only in 1846. (6) The constitution is dated 8 February 1843 (Riograndense page) but 1842 (Ragamuffin War page). (7) Fructuoso Rivera's Uruguayan government gave the rebels financial and indirect military support and 'had the intention of creating a political union' with the republic (Ragamuffin War page): no territory changed. Neighbour slugs: argentine-confederation and oriental-republic-of-uruguay appear in the seed only as border cells; no territorial event with them is on the page.
